note: SNG-232 the Seam Auditor's declared-seam list, authored by Aevi (PO) from THIS session's tickets. Each seam is a REAL producer->consumer contract that broke or is knowingly load-bearing - NOT speculative (the §Guard: a seam check that can't fail is theater; every entry here has a real producer/consumer pair). CCode builds the auditor to check these; the ledger GROWS BY INCIDENT (a future seam bug = one new entry). kinds: field_shape (both ends must agree on TYPE), field_presence (a writer may omit a field a reader assumes -> the reader must floor/guard OR the writer must fill), cross_source (a consumer reads a source a related producer doesn't feed), enum_vocab (op/id vocab must be the SAME set across contract/handler/prompt).

seams.contract: A location read for encounter-eligibility MUST have a usable dangerLevel. A generated location may omit it; the READER must floor null->1 (SNG-225 §4b) AND the writer should fill it on mint (§4a).
seams.brokeAs: SNG-225: gen-waygate had dangerLevel:null -> null read as 0 -> minDanger>0 eliminated all 24 dangerous encounters -> 7/58 eligible, all peaceful. Erik saw 'no encounters on highest setting'.
seams.checkHint: flag any location-reader that does arithmetic/comparison on dangerLevel without a null-floor; assert the mint path assigns dangerLevel.

seams.consumer: the world-position schema + SNG-180 wiring audit + map/travel readers
seams.contract: A location that ships in the manifest MUST have worldPos {colatitude,longitude,depth} and axisVector[12]. A generated or hand-authored location may omit them; the schema+audit must catch it BEFORE ship.
seams.brokeAs: Aevi's the_old_warden_post shipped with worldPos/axisVector null -> broke content_ci across 4 commits. The null was 'schema-valid' as absence until SNG-180 caught it late.
seams.checkHint: assert every manifest-listed location has non-null worldPos+axisVector at content_ci time, not wiring-audit time (catch earlier).

seams.contract: The _gen marker's TYPE must agree: writer sets `_gen:true` (boolean) but a reader guard checked it as an object (presence-not-type). Reader must handle boolean-or-object, or writer must always write the object form.
seams.brokeAs: SNG-216: every gen-location has _gen:true (boolean); the guard expected an object -> threw on travel to any gen-place -> aborted the location commit (the desync root).
seams.checkHint: flag a reader that does property-access on _gen without a typeof guard; or assert the mint writes a consistent _gen shape.

seams.contract: poleIntensity MUST be an object {pole:0..1}, never a float. A content author may write a scalar by mistake.
seams.brokeAs: Aevi's warden_post wrote poleIntensity as a float -> schema fail. The type was wrong, not the value.
seams.checkHint: schema already catches this (object required); the seam entry documents it as a known author-error shape.

seams.consumer: listAvailableEncounters -> the GM's AVAILABLE ENCOUNTERS block (app.js:2010)
seams.contract: The GM-offered encounter block MUST draw from the same source the world actually spawns from. It reads location.encounterSeeds (hand-authored) ONLY; the pool+bestiary are a DIFFERENT source the GM never sees.
seams.brokeAs: SNG-231: newEncounter/encounterOps fired 0 times in 190 turns - the GM's offer-source is encounterSeeds (mostly empty), disconnected from the pool. The rich pool (225) + bestiary (229) are unreachable via GM offer.
seams.checkHint: assert the GM-offer builder reads from the same eligibility source as the tick-path spawn; flag a consumer of encounterSeeds that ignores the pool.

seams.consumer: the intent-parser + skill wheel + resolver (read character.abilities[])
seams.contract: A discovery the player can USE must be registered where usability is READ (abilities[]), not only where discoveries are recorded (discoveries[]). recordDiscovery must ALSO register a usable ability.
seams.brokeAs: SNG-226: Marrow's Wings landed in discoveries[] not abilities[]; the intent-parser reads abilities[], never saw it, refused the action feasible:false. Player earned a skill the game wouldn't let them cast.
seams.checkHint: assert that anything the parser/wheel treats as usable is written to abilities[]; flag a producer of a 'usable' record that writes only to discoveries[].

seams.consumer: the content LOADER (must read provides.bestiary) + any creatureId reference
seams.contract: A manifest key MUST be read by the loader or the content silently doesn't load. provides.bestiary was declared but the loader never read it -> creatureIds don't resolve.
seams.brokeAs: SNG-229: content_ci FAILed 'provides.bestiary is a key the loader never reads (SNG-065)' - all 26 creatures declared-but-not-loaded. The weave's creatureIds pointed at unresolvable content.
seams.checkHint: content_ci already has the SNG-065 check (manifest key must be loader-read); this seam documents it applies to EVERY new provides.* key.

seams.consumer: travelIntentOf trusted-path (mints travelTo as a destination, app.js:4425)
seams.contract: travelTo MUST be a PLACE, never a PERSON. The parser can set it to a person's name; the resolver's trusted-path mints ANY unmapped travelTo as a phantom place, with only a pronoun-guard (NOT_A_PLACE).
seams.brokeAs: SNG-228: 'fly to the brick hall to catch Ossian' set travelTo='Ossian' (a person) -> minted 'Ossian' as a phantom destination ('take the road to Ossian'). The pronoun guard doesn't catch proper-name people.
seams.checkHint: assert the travelTo consumer cross-checks against the NPC registry + this-turn's named people before minting a place; flag a place-mint that trusts travelTo without a person-check.

seams.consumer: any reader looking them up (a top-level character.aspirations read finds nothing)
seams.contract: A reader of aspirations MUST read character.practice.aspirations, not character.aspirations (top-level). The nesting is load-bearing; a wrong-path read returns empty and 'proves' absence.
seams.brokeAs: Aevi read s['aspirations'] top-level (empty) and wrongly told Erik he had none; they live at practice.aspirations (hunters_strike 2/10). The UI showed them; the wrong-path read denied them.
seams.checkHint: documents the canonical path; flag any code/spec reading character.aspirations at top level.

seams.producer: the GM op contract (gm.js op docs) + the handler set (app.js applyTurn) + SALVAGEABLE_OPS
seams.contract: Every op must exist in ALL THREE: the prompt contract (so the model knows it), the handler (so it applies), and the tracked vocab (so a false-zero is distinguishable from a dead path). A documented op with no handler, or a handler with no doc, is a silent dead path.
seams.brokeAs: SNG-190/179 built the emission tracker precisely because ops drifted between these three sets - 'a built op the model never reaches'. The See-the-Machine NOT-EMITTED panel is the runtime symptom of this seam.
seams.checkHint: assert: set(prompt-documented ops) == set(handled ops) == set(tracked vocab); flag any op present in one but not all three (excluding intentionally-internal, marked).

seams.producer: the GM (emits markTeacher/standingOps/offerAcquisition with a traditionId)
seams.consumer: app.js (resolves traditionId against CONTENT.traditionIndex; silently drops unknowns)
seams.contract: A traditionId the GM emits MUST be a real id from THE PEOPLES vocab block, or it's silently discarded. The prompt must SHOW the valid ids (it does, SNG-179) and the handler must not fail-silent without a vocab-miss log.
seams.brokeAs: SNG-179: four ops ask the model for a traditionId; app.js silently dropped anything unresolvable, so markTeacher looked emitted-but-inert. The _opVocabMisses capture exists BECAUSE of this seam.
seams.checkHint: assert the prompt's traditionId vocab block == CONTENT.traditionIndex ids; the handler logs a vocab-miss (already does) rather than fail-silent.

seams.producer: quest content authoring (a quest's stages[] array)
seams.consumer: the quest-detail UI stageRow (app.js:6075, renders s.id/s.title/s.objective)
seams.contract: A quest stage MUST be an OBJECT {id,title,objective,...}, never a plain string. A string stage has no .id/.title, so the UI renders an empty row with a dead 'Mark this stage met' button and a blank radio.
seams.brokeAs: SNG-238: Aevi's 7 bestiary hunts wrote stages as plain strings -> rendered as empty rows + dead radios (Erik's screenshots of The Stag That Won't Die etc). Rebuilt as objects, CI green.
seams.checkHint: assert every quest.stages[] element is an object with id+title (not a string); flag a quest whose stages are strings before it reaches the renderer.

howItGrows: Every future seam bug adds ONE entry here (producer, consumer, contract, brokeAs, checkHint) + one check in the auditor. A seam caught once is caught forever. Start with these 11 (the session's real breaks); do NOT pre-enumerate speculative seams (§Guard: a check that can't fail is theater).
